newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks surge to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks surge to new record close.

text.p: Swiss shares shot to new highs on Friday, extending recent gains, as a four percent jump in index heavyweight Roche drove the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) to a record close.
Stronger U.S. markets also bolstered Swiss stocks.
The SMI closed up 63.1 points, or 1.5 percent, at 4,272.2, after setting an all-time high of 4,272.4 during the session.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gained 38.95 points, or 1.45 percent, to close at the day's high of 2,728.33 which was also a record close.
Roche was again driven by renewed rumours about a possible merger, divestment or a change in its capital structure.
Roche certificates jumped 495 francs, or 4.13 percent, to 12,495 francs. Its strong gains on the cash market lead to soaring demand for SMI futures on the Swiss Soffex exchange.
But a sharp rise in implied volatilities left demand for Roche's options lagging behind demand for its warrants and certificates, a trader said.
Alongside Roche, Novartis registered shares also rose 16 francs to 1,629.
Clariant continued Thursday's strong 1996 sales report, coupled with a positive profit outlook. The shares climbed 18 francs to 684. Ems gained 100 francs to 5,500.
